h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, י״ג Ki Savo, 13
Reading the Rebukes Restores Torah and Peace Before Renewal

p: and those of Mishneh Torah before Rosh Hashanah.
So that the year may end together with its curses.
Granted, those of Mishneh Torah, etc.;
is Atzeres then a New Year?
'And on Atzeres, for the fruits of the tree.'"
it implies that even for the people of the West,
that they complete the Torah in three years,
before Atzeres and before Rosh Hashanah,
just as they read the four parshiyos
and the passages of the festivals.
And it needs to be understood
why he instituted that they read
those of Toras Kohanim before Atzeres
and those of Mishneh Torah before Rosh Hashanah,
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִלָּה לא, ב)
And likewise what they said in the Gemara (Megillah 31b),
'And on Atzeres, for the fruits of the tree'"
though this is only a time
and does not pertain so much to the individual.
עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ז, ב)
based on what they said (Rosh Hashanah 7b):
ו׳ בְּסִיוָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
"The sixth of Sivan is the New Year for the Two Loaves,"
and it brings this from what we learned,
"And on Atzeres, for the fruits of the tree,"
bring the Two Loaves on Atzeres?
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעֲצֶרֶת זְמַן פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן וְכוּלֵּי
Because Atzeres is the time of the fruits of the tree, etc."
better that they read the rebuke
which is also a New Year,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאוֹתָהּ בָּרַיְיתָא (שָׁם ז, ב)
as written in that same Baraisa (ibid. 7b):
"The sixteenth of Nissan is the New Year for the Omer";
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבַּפֶּסַח זְמַן תְּבוּאָה הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
Because Pesach is the time of grain, etc."
And the Omer permits the new grain in the country,
and on Pesach they are judged regarding grain;
so it would be more fitting to say
"let the year end with its curses"
which permits the new grain only in the Mikdash,
and is the time of the fruits of the tree,
which are not as necessary to a person
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר (בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ)
based on what is said (in the Zohar Chadash on this parshah),
that the curses in Toras Kohanim
and the curses in Mishneh Torah
Now regarding the destruction of the First Temple
עַל עָזְבָם אֶת תּוֹרָתִי (יִרְמְיָה ט, יא–יב)
And regarding the destruction of the Second Temple
where they occupied themselves with Torah,
Because there was baseless hatred in it."
Now all the blessings and curses
that they are not for reward and punishment;
for if so, it should rather have made known
the reward and punishments of the World to Come,
that if they improve their ways,
Hashem, may He be blessed, will send them
all the assistance of every kind of good,
so that they can fulfill the whole Torah
(and so wrote the Rambam, of blessed memory,
if they do not walk in the way of Hashem,
then the punishments, Heaven forfend, will come
"But he who loves him disciplines him early" (Mishlei 13:24),
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרְרוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בִּתְשׁוּבָה
so that they be aroused thereby to teshuvah;
וּכְאָב אֶת בֵּן יִרְצֶה (שָׁם ג, יב)
"and as a father the son in whom he delights" (ibid. 3:12),
who raises the rod and frightens him
so that he improve his way.
And Ezra instituted that they read
which is the time of the Giving of the Torah,
"so that the year may end with its curses"
they will be aroused to teshuvah
in the destruction of the First Temple,
and for this the time is Atzeres,
which is the time of the Giving of the Torah.
to read the curses of Mishneh Torah,
in order to rectify the blemish of baseless hatred.
And in truth they are one,
and peace is called the attribute of Yosef;
as it is written of Yosef,
וַיַּכֵּר יוֹסֵף אֶת אֶחָיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, ח)
when he fell into their hand,
וְהוּא שֶׁמִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִדַּת שָׁלוֹם
that is, one who has the attribute of peace
it is a sign that he is clean in the attribute of tzaddik.
וְכֵן הָיָה סִיבַּת כָּל הַגָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם
And so the cause of the entire exile of Egypt
was that he spoke against them
to the daughters of the land;
and presumably it seemed so to him,
and they, who knew that they were clean of this,
of not being clean in this attribute,
and "whoever disqualifies, disqualifies with his own blemish"
And therefore they sold him as a slave,
that they said, "Let us go and follow
was he not cursed with slavery?"
And the sin of Cham, the father of Canaan,
was in the blemish of the covenant,
for he had relations in the Ark
and he was smitten in his skin,
וְהָיָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן פָּגוּם בָּזֶה
and he too was blemished in this.
And likewise one opinion says he sodomized him
And so Yosef was clarified in Egypt
in his attribute, "tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
and all Yisrael were fenced in through his merit
And truth and peace are one
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 12b):
that truth and peace are bound one with the other;
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רמב, א)
and so it is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 242a):
"Body and covenant we count as one."
accused against the creation of the world,
Peace said, 'Let him not be created,
What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do?
He took truth and cast it to the ground, etc."
what was done about the accusation of peace.
אַךְ אֱמֶת וְשָׁלוֹם קְשִׁיר דָּא בְּדָא
But truth and peace are bound one with the other:
for whenever the intent is in the way of truth,
for they are like one man with one heart.
And the main cause of strife
in the dispute of Shammai and Hillel:
to teach you that affection and friendship
are of the seed of Yisrael,
which is Yaakov, the aspect of truth,
are called by the name of Yosef,
which is the attribute of peace.

p: it is brought in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36):
of which it is said, 'And it was the day.'"
and at the Splitting of the Sea it is brought
nevertheless the light was hidden from them
They went out into the wilderness
to behold the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.,
דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְּרֵי וְכוּלֵּי
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah, etc."
For there, at the Splitting of the Sea,
although there was a revelation of Atika,
it was only in the aspect of seeing:
how much they would be able to merit
at the Giving of the Torah as an acquisition
(as explained on the festival of Pesach, maamar 40).
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come, said,
that the seeing at the Splitting of the Sea
was like the strength of chassidus at its beginning;
and they say in the name of the Rebbe, Reb Bunim,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
that it is only on loan,
כִּי לֹא מֵחָכְמָה שָׁאַלְתָּ זֹאת (קֹהֶלֶת ז, י)
"For it is not out of wisdom that you ask this" (Koheles 7:10).
when they merited what is said,
פָּנִים בְּפָנִים דִּיבֶּר ה׳ עִמָּכֶם (דְּבָרִים ה, ד)
"Face to face Hashem spoke with you" (Devarim 5:4).
they are forbidden leaven and chametz,
so that there not rule over them
and on Shavuos, with the Two Loaves,
since the yetzer hara had already been nullified,
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו)
and were it not for the damage afterward,
there would then have been the true rectification,
as before the damage of Adam HaRishon.
And therefore the Two Loaves come
of which a little is good
and this is what will remain of the yetzer hara
so that there be desire for Torah;
as written in the Midrash HaNe'elam
"For were it not for the yetzer hara,
the joy of Torah study would not exist."
And therefore Ezra did not institute
of Toras Kohanim be read before Pesach,
which is the New Year for the Omer,
"that the year may end with its curses";
for then they could not rectify
so as to merit as they merited then,
since that was only from the kindness of Hashem;
גַּם לֹא הָיָה רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה
And therefore he instituted to read them
which is the New Year for the Two Loaves,
that then "the year will end with its curses";
that is, through reading the passage
they will be aroused and merit to rectify
the blemish that caused the destruction of the First Temple,
which was "because they forsook My Torah."
And Atzeres is the time of the Giving of the Torah,
and every year when the time comes,
that was at the time of the Giving of the Torah;
the true rectification had not yet come;
so that through this they will merit to rectify,
and the year will end with its curses.

p: which is the time of fear and teshuvah,
of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur
begin, "And so, place Your fear, etc."
for it is the time of judgment
and is propitious to bring fear into the heart;
and this is the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik,
אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח)
"And may they all form a single band
to do Your will with a whole heart";
for whenever the aim will be
automatically they will all form a single band,
like one man with one heart,
of Mishneh Torah be read before Rosh Hashanah;
דְּאִיתָא בְּלִיקּוּטֵי תּוֹרָה מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
for it is brought in Likkutei Torah from the Arizal, of blessed memory,
that the curses of Mishneh Torah
are for the rectification of the blemish of the covenant,
and he wrote that the number ninety-eight is aimed at this.
And through the reading of the passage
to rectify the blemish of baseless hatred;
the attribute of Yosef, as mentioned above,
they will merit the attribute of peace,
"and they will all form a single band
to do Your will with a whole heart."
And they read this on Shabbosos,
for Shabbos is a time of Torah,
"All agree that the Torah was given on Shabbos";
and Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 92a);
therefore then is the time to rectify this.
And when there are two Shabbosos
but they do not divide Matos and Masei,
that we wish to make a break
and to read on one Shabbos
a parshah that does not speak of curses;
that Shabbos is the sum of all blessings,
that comes in the week after it
is contained in the preceding Shabbos,
"and You sanctified it above all the seasons."
And every Shabbos that precedes the festival
contains within it the holiness of the festival
that will come after it on the weekdays.
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come, said,
that this is why the Shabbos before Pesach is called
and it is the first of the festivals,
and therefore the Shabbos before it is called
And likewise, on the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah
there is already contained in it
and then already "the year begins with its blessings."
And therefore they read on the Shabbos
the passage of curses of Mishneh Torah,
and then it will be "let the year end with its curses";
which is the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah,
it will be "let the year begin with its blessings."
